lang_dao: Lãng Đào Môn, ferry families of the Nine-Bend River: coats of oiled river-green or tar-black cloth, tightly woven and kept clean and glossy by the oil; wide straw hats hung at the back or worn; sleeves pushed to the elbow; bare feet on deck; a boat-pole, rope coil or tin lamp close by. Inner disciples tie a green headcloth, outer disciples a plain brown one; elders' coats have small bronze fittings. No embroidery.
thoi_tinh: Thối Tinh Môn, smiths of an iron mountain: black felt aprons over well-cut dark grey-brown tunics of heavy cloth, sleeves cut short to show forearms shaved bare against sparks, a leather thumb-ring of iron for the tongs; clean, sturdy and fitted, charcoal-dark with faint rust-orange at the hems; the head's apron is edged in red-brown leather. Hands are always blackened at the nails.
tam_kiem: Tầm Kiếm Đường, mountain hunters and cave-searchers: well-made hunters' leathers in forest brown and moss green over a plain linen shirt, a short quilted jerkin, rope coiled over one shoulder, a flat map case on a strap, a sword with a notch-filed crossguard (one filed notch per cave searched); clean, mended with neat stitches, nothing bright.
trac_anh: Trạc Anh Đài, seal and whale hunters of the frost coast: tunics of tightly sewn sealskin and dark waxed wool in sea-grey and black, collars closed with pale walrus-ivory toggles, cloth hat-strings tied under the chin (the terrace's old song), sleeves cut close for rowing; clean, well-fitted, damp-dark at the shoulders; no jewellery but a carved ivory toggle.
